keyboardHelp.title: Paint on the field
keyboardHelp.moveCursorSlower: Move the cursor in smaller steps

preferences.title: Simulation
preferences.resolutionHelp: Finer grids resolve more structure and need more GPU work. Takes effect when a screen is reloaded.

controls.fieldHelp: Move the paint cursor with the arrow keys, hold shift for finer steps, then press space or enter to paint.
controls.fieldReadOnlyHelp: The temperature field. Use the controls to change what is shown.
controls.anisotropy: Ratio of conductivity along x to conductivity along y
controls.edges: Behaviour of the field at the edges of the plate
controls.probeHelp: Drag the probe over the field to read the temperature at a point.
controls.clearField: Return the temperature field to its starting state without changing the other controls

screenSummary.playArea: A square plate whose colour shows its temperature at every point. Painting with the heat or cool brush changes the temperature where you paint.
screenSummary.controlArea: Controls choose whether the brush heats or cools, set its size, turn isotherm lines on and off, and reset the plate.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Paint on the plate to make hot and cold regions, then read the temperature with the probe.

temperature.currentDetails: The plate ranges from {{min}} to {{max}} degrees Celsius.

controls.isotherms: Draw lines joining points at the same temperature

screenSummary.playArea: A plate of a chosen material, with its temperature shown as colour and the heat flux shown as arrows pointing from hot toward cold.
screenSummary.controlArea: Controls choose the material, set the behaviour of the plate edges, select which layers are drawn, and place a cross-section line.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Paint a hot spot, then watch the arrows and see how much faster heat spreads through copper than through glass.

conduction.currentDetails: The plate ranges from {{min}} to {{max}} degrees Celsius.

controls.crossSection: Show a line across the plate and graph the temperature along it

screenSummary.playArea: A plate carrying both a temperature field and a velocity field. Tracer particles drift with the flow, carrying warm and cool regions with them.
screenSummary.controlArea: Controls choose the flow pattern, set the flow speed, and select which layers are drawn.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Paint a hot spot into the flow and watch it be carried along as well as spreading out.

convection.currentDetails: The plate ranges from {{min}} to {{max}} degrees Celsius.

controls.flowPreset: Choose the shape of the velocity field

screenSummary.playArea: A plate where heat both diffuses through the material and is carried by a flow. The balance between the two is adjustable.
screenSummary.controlArea: A transport control shifts between diffusion-dominated and advection-dominated behaviour, with the resulting Péclet number displayed. Layer checkboxes choose what is drawn.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Move the transport control and watch the same hot spot change from spreading evenly to being swept downstream.

combined.currentDetails: The plate ranges from {{min}} to {{max}} degrees Celsius. The Péclet number is {{peclet}}.

controls.transport: Shift between diffusion-dominated and advection-dominated transport

screenSummary.playArea: A plate whose material can differ from place to place. Painting material into the plate builds composites, barriers, and channels for heat.
screenSummary.controlArea: Controls choose which material the brush paints, how anisotropic it is, and which layers are drawn.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Paint a strip of insulator across the plate, then paint a hot spot on one side and watch heat go around the barrier.

materials.currentDetails: The plate ranges from {{min}} to {{max}} degrees Celsius.

controls.anisotropyHelp: Values above one let heat travel more easily left and right; values below one favour up and down
